methodological_rigor.justification: Manuscript file too large to complete read. Based on accessible portion: phase I/IIa trial assessing drug sensitivity profiling (DSP) in 96 pediatric solid tumors. Quality control criteria applied (high/intermediate vs. borderline/fail quality screens). However, small sample sizes per tumor type (Wilms n=3 with SIX1 mutation), exploratory nature without pre-specified hypotheses, and limited statistical power for biomarker discovery evident. Missing details on statistical methods for comparisons between genotypes.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Exploratory functional biomarker discovery study in pediatric solid tumors. LoE 4: case series/mechanistic reasoning. Clinical relevance limited: identifies potential biomarker associations (SIX1/MEKi, BCL2 inhibitor sensitivity) requiring functional validation before clinical application. No prospective clinical trial data.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensively detailed for DSP protocols and bioinformatics pipelines. Supplementary materials referenced extensively. However, INFORM registry data access restricted; no explicit data sharing statement for code/processed data. Reproducibility limited by proprietary DSP platform.

novelty_literature.justification: Integration of DSP with multiomics in pediatric solid tumors addresses gap in pediatric precision medicine. SIX1 mutation association with MEKi sensitivity novel for Wilms tumors. However, findings hypothesis-generating requiring functional validation.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear methods and logical presentation. Figures communicating drug sensitivity clustering and pathway analyses effective. Discussion appropriately highlights need for functional validation. File size limited complete assessment.

key_strengths: Novel integration of DSP with multiomics (MOFA+) in pediatric solid tumors
Identification of SIX1 mutation-MEKi sensitivity association in Wilms tumors
Mechanistic network analysis (CARNIVAL) linking molecular alterations to drug response
key_concerns: Very small sample size (only 3 SIX1-mutant Wilms tumors) limits robustness
Exploratory findings require functional validation (knockdown/overexpression studies)
No prospective clinical trial data; hypothesis-generating only
CARNIVAL network analysis computational; mechanism speculative
File read incomplete; full assessment limited
chief_reviewer.rationale: Early-phase exploratory biomarker discovery study requiring functional validation. Suitable for Tier 4 with major revisions addressing mechanistic studies and prospective clinical validation strategy.
